# Accessibility

_Effective October 9, 2026_

We want Longstead to be usable by as many people as possible. This page says plainly what is supported and what is not.

## What is supported
- **Text size.** The app uses system text styles for most text, and has an in-app **Text size** control (Settings) with steps from Small up to the five Accessibility sizes (Accessibility 1 to 5). The default is "Large", which is the iOS standard size.
- **VoiceOver.** Icon-only buttons (Back, Settings, More options, Close, text-size buttons, plan selection) have spoken labels. Charts have a VoiceOver summary instead of exposing every drawing element: the fan chart (with a description of the selected point), the timeline strip, the stacked-bar chart, the donut, the stacked bar, and the sparkline each read as a single labeled item. Decorative icons are hidden from VoiceOver. Section titles are marked as headings. Advisor activity ("Advisor is working") is announced.
- **Reduce Motion.** Animated elements check the system Reduce Motion setting.
- **Color.** The palette is defined for light and dark appearances. In dark mode (see below) the main text (contrast about 18.7:1 on the background), secondary text (about 8.9:1), and the accent color (about 7.7:1) meet WCAG AA and AAA for normal text.
- **Keyboard and Mac.** The Mac app is a native macOS app with a menu bar (including New Project, Command-N), so standard macOS keyboard navigation and VoiceOver apply.
- **Voice input.** The advisor chat is compatible with the system dictation keyboard and the Apple Intelligence listening tips the app links to.

## Known gaps
- **System text size on iPhone.** On iPhone the app sets its own text size from the in-app control, which defaults to Large, instead of following the system Dynamic Type setting automatically. People who use a larger system size need to raise it once in Settings. iPad and Mac follow the system.
- **Fixed-size text.** A few elements use fixed point sizes (some icons and a handful of labels in Settings, chat, and the legal screens) and do not scale with text size.
- **Appearance.** The app currently forces a dark appearance and does not follow the system light setting. People who need light mode or high contrast may find it harder to read. The light palette is defined but not used.
- **Lower-contrast captions.** Tertiary caption text in dark mode has a contrast ratio of about 4.2:1 (and about 4.0:1 on cards), which is below the 4.5:1 target for small text.
- **Color alone.** We have not audited whether gains and losses are ever conveyed by color alone.
- **Increase Contrast, Differentiate Without Color, and Bold Text** settings are not specifically handled.
- **Charts** give a summary rather than a navigable data table; there is no audio graph.
- **AI answers** are generated text and may not be consistently structured for screen readers; AI tools can also be wrong (see the AI Disclaimer).
- **Languages.** The app is in English only. Right-to-left layouts and localization have not been tested.
- **Orientation.** iPhone is portrait only.
- **Apple Intelligence** features depend on the device and language Apple supports.
- We have not completed testing with Switch Control, Voice Control, or Full Keyboard Access.

## Tell us
If something is hard to use, email **wavypix@gmail.com** with "Accessibility" in the subject, the app version, your device and OS, and the assistive technology you use. We will try to reply within 5 business days and to prioritize fixes.
